correctness.rationale: Independent sign/magnitude representation, fourth-cumulant expansion and a law-of-total-variance closure reconstruct both conditional formulas for every n>=2; positive coefficient B follows by the independent-copy identity. Exact-rational exhaustive enumerator checks 516 comparisons for several nontrivial laws. Finite checks are corroborative only.

originality.rationale: Comparison of the actual conditional scatter and sign-count statements with the classical binomial sign test, spacing-based tests for symmetry, half-normal moment formulas and accessible statistical records found no same statement or stronger theorem implying all these conditional mean/variance and explained-variance identities. The closest author-hosted manuscript was examined in its main sections and appendix. This is a qualified originality assessment, not a claim to have ruled out every general quadratic-form moment theorem.
residual_risks: General results on moments of quadratic forms with independent sign and magnitude components might imply the formulas without naming sign count; such full literature was not exhausted.
The 1946 sign-test paper and the 2014 half-normal reference were not read in full; no claim of full-document exclusion is made.
Finding novelty is a qualified literature comparison rather than proof of global uniqueness.

value.rationale: The relation between sign-based tests and observed dispersion has motivated statistical interest. The theorem gives an exact universal nonlinear conditional mean and a strict variance-ordering boundary for all symmetric finite-fourth-moment laws, including a diagnostic quantitative R-squared; mere zero linear covariance does not detect this dependence. A deterministic-magnitude equality boundary and Gaussian benchmark make the claim structurally informative rather than a single numerical substitution.
